translationRepairs: Book of Sui, 54th year of Volume, 19th year of Biography

s0001 reads 隋書卷五十四列傳第十九; 卷 and 列傳 mark volume and biography numbers, so “54th year of Volume / 19th year of Biography” invents reign-year counters the Chinese does not have, and the proposed wording matches the source.
His grandfather Pi had been Wei’s grand preceptor.
His grandfather Pi had been Wei's Grand Commandant.
s0004 has 魏太尉; 太尉 is Grand Commandant, distinct from 太師 Grand Preceptor, so the idiomatic “grand preceptor” is a wrong office and the proposed Grand Commandant is accurate.
His grandfather Pi was Grand Preceptor of Wei.
His grandfather Pi was Grand Commandant of Wei.
The same 太尉 in s0004 must be Grand Commandant in the literal field; “Grand Preceptor” is the English for 太師, not for this office.
Changshu had dignified bearing even as a child. At eight, Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him and marveled, saying, "Duke Wang has this grandson—that alone is enough to make his line immortal."
Changshu had dignified bearing even as a child. At eight, Zhou Taizu saw him and marveled, saying, "Duke Wang has this grandson—that alone is enough to make his line immortal."
s0006 has 周太祖見而異之; 周太祖 is Zhou Taizu (Yuwen Tai), not Emperor Wu (武帝), so the idiomatic substitution invents the wrong ruler.
From childhood Changshu had dignified bearing. At eight years of age, Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him and was struck by him, saying: "The Duke Wang has this grandson; that is enough for immortality."
From childhood Changshu had dignified bearing. At eight years of age, Zhou Taizu saw him and was struck by him, saying: "The Duke Wang has this grandson; that is enough for immortality."
The same 周太祖 in s0006 requires Zhou Taizu in the literal field; “Emperor Wu of Zhou” misidentifies the person named in the Chinese.
Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he entered service as a thousand-ox guard attendant and was enfeoffed as duke of Huairen county.
Under Zhou Taizu he entered service as a thousand-ox guard attendant and was enfeoffed as duke of Huairen county.
s0035 opens 周太祖時; that is the time of Zhou Taizu, not of Emperor Wu, so the idiomatic “Under Emperor Wu of Zhou” is a factual misidentification.
In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, he left commoner status as Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant and was enfeoffed as Duke of Huairen County.
In the time of Zhou Taizu, he left commoner status as Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant and was enfeoffed as Duke of Huairen County.
Literal “In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou” likewise contradicts s0035’s 周太祖時; Zhou Taizu is the correct referent.
first year of In of Kaihuang, again as campaign commander, he suppressed rebellious tribes and pacified them.
In the first year of Kaihuang, again as campaign commander, he suppressed rebellious tribes and pacified them.
s0042 begins 開皇元年, “the first year of Kaihuang”; the garbled “first year of In of Kaihuang” is not English supported by the Chinese, and the proposed phrasing restores the date formula.
